solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Complained about unfilled pothole in road

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: in says the pick from pothole goes inside the abbreviation for road
an unfilled word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a pothole in the road that the council never filled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfilled' strips a word to its outer letters; 'about' is the Latin circa, a common abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault and grumble, so carped is a synonym of complained.

clue.text: A desire that's excessive? Yes

parts.note: greed is excessive desire for more

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question asking whether wanting too much is greedy, answered with a simple yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a reply, the word signals assent exactly as yes does.

clue.text: Agenda against the ounce, presumably?

definitions.meaning: a list or plan of items to be dealt with
someone opposed to the imperial ounce is presumably in favour (pro) of the metric gram, spelt gramme in Britain

explanation.surface: A political agenda opposing the ounce, as if weights and measures were a campaign issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as PRO GRAMME: being for the gramme suggests being against the ounce, its imperial rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of events or business to be got through is an agenda, the usual sense of the plan word.

clue.text: Sadly, end involved swallowing one's pride?

indicators.note: swallowing says the jumbled letters take the next piece inside them
involved means intricately tangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Sadly, a story ends with someone having to swallow their pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' is the anagram signal and 'swallowing' puts I inside the result; the question mark shows pride is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride is one of the seven deadly sins of Christian teaching, so it is given as an example.

clue.text: Deficit in fuel is massive

indicators.note: in places the shortfall word inside the fuel word

parts.note: coal is a fuel
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A huge shortfall in fuel supplies, as in an energy crisis report.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something enormous in size, so they are straight synonyms.

clue.text: Boots perhaps mostly seen with European woman's garment

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: Boots is a British high-street pharmacy chain, so an example of a pharmacist's shop

explanation.surface: Footwear seen with a European woman's outfit, as in a fashion note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boots' looks like footwear but is the British chemist chain; 'mostly' drops its last letter, giving CHEMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift or loose dress worn by women, often as underwear, is called by this French-derived name.

clue.text: See, teacher upset tree-dweller

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a teacher who has been upset by something in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This slow-moving nocturnal primate lives in trees in South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Not all glamorous ambassadors dance

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some, but not all, of the glamorous diplomats are dancing at the embassy party.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Brazilian ballroom form is a well-known kind of dance.

clue.text: Give up salt, a diet counsellor initially ordered

parts.note: a salt is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so these letters are rearranged
initially takes just the opening letter of the word counsellor

explanation.surface: A counsellor tells someone to give up salt and go on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is an old sailor, AB; 'ordered' rearranges A, DIET and C (from 'counsellor initially') into DICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce a throne or a responsibility is to give it up formally.

clue.text: Claim Yorkshire town lacks aspiration

indicators.note: lacks says a letter is missing from the town name

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England
an aspirate is the breathy sound of the letter H

explanation.surface: Someone claims that a Yorkshire town has no ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition but means the H sound, dropped as when a speaker leaves off an initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay claim to something without right is to take it for oneself, as in arrogating powers.

clue.text: Prepared, with me going in for a treatment

indicators.note: going in for means taking the place of, so one letter is swapped out for the new pair

parts.note: prepared means ready

explanation.surface: Someone feels ready now they have signed up for a medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in for' looks like undergoing a procedure, but it means replacing the A in READY with ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure or medicine for an illness is a treatment for it.

clue.text: Reptile saving one exotic bird

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the remaining letters are rearranged
saving means except, so a letter is left out

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A reptile rescuing an unusual bird, like a wildlife documentary scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like rescuing but means except: REPTILE without I leaves REPTLE, which 'exotic' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This seabird, such as the storm species, is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Fashionable point of view, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a stance is a position or attitude on an issue

explanation.surface: A trendy opinion offered up as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A case cited as an illustration is an example, as in the phrase for example.

clue.text: Moreover, nearly all saw?

indicators.note: nearly all means everything but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a saw is a tool

explanation.surface: A question about whether almost everyone saw something as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see, but it is the cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition or as well, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Food that by implication could be too apt?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the second word of the dish signals an anagram of its first word, and the letters of the potato word, once mashed, can spell too apt

explanation.surface: A dish described as maybe being a little too fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, 'mashed' as an anagram signal on POTATO, gives TOO APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of boiled tubers crushed with butter and milk is a familiar food.

clue.text: Dictator's supreme rule

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone who dictates, speaking words out loud, so what is spoken is a soundalike

parts.note: supreme means chief or main, as principal does

explanation.surface: A dictator's rule is absolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant but is one dictating, signalling the soundalike of PRINCIPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundamental law or guiding standard is a rule that governs conduct.

clue.text: Money handler wants safe in back, after short time

indicators.note: after says the second part follows the first

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: in places the safe word inside the back word

parts.note: the rear is the back
sure means safe, as in sure footing

explanation.surface: A money handler wants a safe at the back of the office, after a brief wait.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who looks after an organisation's funds is the one handling its money.

clue.text: One composer or another wanting daughter to support sibling

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support means to sit underneath the other piece

parts.note: sib is short for sibling

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: another composer is Frederick Delius, the English composer

explanation.surface: A family story of a composer whose daughter must look after a brother or sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is a second composer, DELIUS; without D it gives ELIUS, which goes under SIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Sibelius was the great Finnish composer of Finlandia, so he is one composer.

clue.text: Turn out as the Sun is expected to do?

definitions.meaning: to turn out is to get out of bed, a call to get up

definitions.text: as the Sun is expected to do?
definitions.meaning: each morning the sun comes up and gives light

explanation.surface: A wake-up call likened to the sun coming up each day.
explanation.definitionFit: This cheery phrase is said to rouse someone from bed, which is to turn out in the morning.

clue.text: One is evenly matched

indicators.note: evenly picks the letters in even positions of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone is described as an even match for a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly matched' looks like a phrase, but 'evenly' takes letters 2, 4 and 6 of 'matched'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cards the top single-pip card counts as one, so the two words share that number.

clue.text: It's posh cooking, one argues plausibly

indicators.note: cooking means preparing or fiddling with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smooth talker defends fancy cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A person using clever but fallacious reasoning is someone who argues plausibly rather than soundly.

clue.text: Mum is retrogressing fast

indicators.note: retrogressing means going backwards, so the little word is read in reverse

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A mother is falling back quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother but means quiet; 'fast' looks like quick but is LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum means saying nothing, so mum means quiet and wordless.

clue.text: Tailless insectivore, first among perils for fly near the ground

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the hedgehog is a spiny animal that eats insects

indicators.note: first among takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A hedgehog without a tail is among the dangers faced by a fly close to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like an insect the insectivore might eat, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots who skim fields at very low altitude, popping over hedges, are said to fly in this way.

clue.text: Restaurant or some bars?

definitions.meaning: a ... room is an eating place serving ... food
a grating is a framework of metal bars

explanation.definitionFit: A grill is both an eating place specialising in grilled food and a set of metal bars over a window or fire.

clue.text: Island hotel put up capital

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means turned so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Iona is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An island hotel builds up the capital of a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like building or giving lodging, but reverses IONA plus H.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Vietnam.

clue.text: Realise murderer must keep quiet

indicators.note: must keep means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone realises a murderer must stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Realise' looks like understand, but it means convert to money.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it into money, which is what this phrasal verb means.

clue.text: Artist, a towering figure around Italy

indicators.note: around says the giant word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a titan is a person of great stature, from the giants of Greek myth
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An artist hailed as a giant of the Italian scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter, so he is an artist.

clue.text: Troublemaker backed old- fashioned businessman

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: retro means old-fashioned in style

explanation.surface: A troublemaker supported a dated businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like supported, but reverses RETRO to give ORTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who brings goods in from abroad is a kind of businessman.

clue.text: Possibly last page is introduction to Michelangelo's David?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: last and is are taken as written, with page shortened to P, its standard abbreviation

indicators.note: introduction to takes the opening letter of the name that follows

explanation.surface: Perhaps the final page introduces Michelangelo's famous statue of David.
explanation.walkthrough: 'David' looks like the sculpture but is King David, traditional author of the Psalms; the question mark shows he is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms, so he is the best-known example of a psalm writer.

clue.text: In time, traitor will make mistakes

indicators.note: In says the traitor goes inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: Eventually a traitor will slip up.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors added to a book; the Latin plural of erratum means mistakes.
